title: Cap. II: Pelagian opening — free will alone; election from foresight holiness
pass_a_gloss: That such a preceding thing is given, upon which the decree of election always rests, human reason blinded by love of itself pretends, Scripture crying out against it. That British serpent vomited forth this dogma full of poison and pestilence: That a human is able by the sole powers of his free choice to keep the law of God, to arrive at eternal life. To this he joined that other of the same virulence: namely that God, foresighting who would live holy through the choice of their will, elected all those unto glory before the foundations of the world were laid. Key lemmas: praecedaneum (preceding ground); Britannus coluber (British serpent = Pelagius); liberum arbitrium (free choice); praescientia sanctitatis (foresight of holiness).
pass_b_english: Blinded self-love in human reason claims there is always some prior ground on which the decree of election rests — and Scripture cries against it. That British serpent spat out this poison: that a person can keep God's law and reach eternal life by free choice alone. He joined to it another venom of the same kind: that God, foresighting who would live holy by their own will's choice, elected them all to glory before the world's foundations were laid.
source_text: Dari tale aliquod praecedaneum, cui semper innitatur decretum electionis, humana ratio amore sui occaecata praetendit, Scriptura reclamante. Britannus ille coluber hoc plenum veneni & pestilentiae dogma evomuit, Posse hominem solis viribus liberi sui arbitrii legem Dei servare, ad vitam aeternam pervenire. Huic & illud alterum conjunxit ejusdem virulentiae, Deum scilicet praevidentem quinam essent per voluntatis suae arbitrium sancte victuri, eos omnes ante jacta mundi fundamenta ad gloriam elegisse.
